term: moves per accidens (κατὰ συμβεβηκὸς κινεῖν), Aristotle's per accidens mover
definition: One moves a thing per accidens when one is a mover of it only in a way, as the one who pulls away a supporting pillar or takes the stone off a wineskin in water (Physics VIII.4, 255b24-27). Lean: the primitive `MovesPerAccidensIn`, kept apart from `MovesIn`. This is Aristotle's per accidens moving of one thing, not Aquinas' per accidens ordered series (DEF-PER-ACCIDENS-ORDERED-SERIES).
